rows.Requirement Title: Addressing Development and Use of Chemical and Biological Weapons by Russia
rows.Requirement Description: Engage subject matter experts with biological, biotechnology, chemical, pharmaceutical manufacturers and distributors to reduce their risk of transactions with sanctioned or trade-restricted entities linked to Russia’s WMD programs. Use commercial trade data to identify and disrupt illicit procurement methods in supply chains.

rows.Requirement Title: Countering Biological Weapons Threats and Protecting U.S. Biotechnology
rows.Requirement Description: Provision SMEs, develop and implement international trainings to 1) strengthen biosecurity, cybersecurity, physical security, personnel reliability, and research oversight measures to protect biological weapon (BW)-applicable materials, sensitive data, U.S. and allies' biotechnologies, equipment, and scientific expertise from theft and/or misuse, 2) engage academic institutions and biotechnology firms on Know-Your-Customer/Investor to prevent adversarial capital investment and acquisition of data/intellectual property, 3) demonstrate U.S. biotechnology leadership by establishing public-private partnerships and promoting U.S. backed standards and best practices for biosecurity, cybersecurity, data security, and intellectual property protection, and 4) perform targeted upgrades to strengthen laboratory physical security, biosecurity, and cybersecurity to secure weaponizable pathogens and BW-applicable materials and sensitive data.

rows.Requirement Title: Countering Chemical Weapons Threats
rows.Requirement Description: CTR’s Chemical Security Program (CSP) is a counterproliferation initiative that prevents U.S. adversaries from acquiring materials, equipment, and expertise for chemical weapons (CW) programs. CSP works with frontline countries to identify, interdict, and investigate high-risk chemical transfers, enforce U.S. sanctions, and promote chemical security standards. The program disrupts efforts to weaponize pharmaceutical-based agents, builds partner capacity to recognize and attribute CW attacks, and prevents illicit chemical shipments. CSP also fosters coordination between partner governments and private industry to strengthen counterproliferation efforts. Through targeted, preventive programming, CSP closes security gaps exploited by adversaries, enhances U.S. and partner resilience, and supports global chemical security while minimizing burdens on legitimate business.

rows.Requirement Title: Countering Chinese and Russian Proliferation of Advanced Conventional Weapons
rows.Requirement Description: Disrupt Chinese and Russian efforts to manufacture, sell, or distribute their existing advanced conventional weapons systems for the purposes of increasing their arsenals, financial revenues, and influence over other countries decision-making processes. CTR will engage subject matter experts with partner governments, private companies, and financial stakeholders to reduce their risks to Russian and CCP illicit procurement of advanced conventional weapon components, private military and security companies, and critical mineral supply chains.

rows.Requirement Title: Countering Iran and DPRK’s WMD, Nuclear, Ballistic Missile, and Drone Proliferation
rows.Requirement Description: The Counterproliferation and Sanctions Enforcement (CASE) program is ACN’s programmatic tool to implement Maximum Pressure on Iran (NSPM-2) and increase global capacity to implement U.S. and international sanctions imposed on Iran and DPRK. CASE equips governments and private sector leaders to detect, disrupt and prevent Iranian and DPRK sanctions evasion activities that enable their acquisition of proliferation sensitive technologies, materials, and expertise, thwarting these nations’ abilities to develop ballistic missile, drone and unmanned aerial systems, and nuclear capabilities that pose a threat to U.S. national security. CASE activities strengthen maritime security, cybersecurity, and global sanctions regimes; disrupt Iran and DPRK revenue generation; and protect U.S. supply chains, U.S. companies’ global investments, and U.S. access to international markets.

rows.Requirement Title: Countering U.S. Adversary WMD and Drone Threats in Iraq
rows.Requirement Description: ACN/CTR Iraq program strengthens Iraq's ability to counter Iranian-backed proxies and terrorist groups by disrupting their access to unmanned aerial systems and WMD, including chemical and biological weapons.  Through targeted support to Iraqi military, law enforcement, and laboratories this program enhances detection and response to UAS and CBW threats in support of NSPM-2.  These efforts protect U.S. personnel and interests in Iraq and the region, weaken Iran's proxy networks, and bolsters U.S. leverage in negotiations on Iran's nuclear program.

rows.Requirement Title: Denying U.S. Adversaries Access to Sensitive Nuclear, Missile, and Advanced Technical Expertise for Weapons of Mass Destruction Programs that Threaten America
rows.Requirement Description: In direct support of NSPM-3, this program provides focused, near-term national security engagements to civilian scientists, technicians, and engineers (STE) with nuclear, missile, and other advanced WMD-relevant technical expertise who are geographically displaced or otherwise rendered financially vulnerable to exploitation by China, Iran, North Korea, or other U.S. adversaries, who seek their expertise for illicit WMD programs meant to threaten American lives and the American homeland.

rows.Requirement Title: Enforcing Sanctions on China and Russia
rows.Requirement Description: Leverage subject matter experts to engage with public and private sector entities to support identification and disruption of complex Chinese and Russian sanctions evasion networks in particularly vulnerable jurisdictions. Contrary to public assurances, China is now the primary supplier of financial and technological components critical to the continued manufacturing of advanced conventional weapons that are critical to Russia and other proliferator states of concern. These targeted engagements provide tools and training to key stakeholders who are motivated to de-risk from Chinese investments and can exert pressure on other sectors, even in countries where governments are friendly to CCP and Russian interests. CTR uses the latest trade data to understand and adapt to the latest sanction evasion strategies.

rows.Requirement Title: Preventing U.S. Adversaries’ Access to Critical Technologies, Exploitation of Scientific and Commercial Facilities for Military Advancement, and international adoption of critical technologies that threaten national and economic security.
rows.Requirement Description: In support of NSPM-3, America's AI Action Plan, and National Security objectives, this NOFO will provision SMEs, develop and implement international trainings to 1) strengthen research security, intellectual property (IP) protection, cybersecurity, physical security, and personnel reliability to protect advanced technologies, including AI, quantum, and semiconductors, and related data and IP from theft or forced transfer, 2) improve space infrastructure and facility inspections to identify dual-use equipment and activities and avoid predatory contracting tactics, and 3) raise awareness of dual-use risks of adopting Chinese critical technologies such as AI, low earth orbit satellites, and smart city technology and improve partner security measures to attract U.S. investment and expand America’s commercial market share.

rows.Requirement Title: Unleashing American Energy Dominance and Expediting Responsible and Secure U.S. Small Modular Reactor (SMR) Deployment through the FIRST Program
rows.Requirement Description: To advance the President's E.Os 14299 and 14154, FIRST harnesses the power of the U.S. nuclear industry to reclaim American global nuclear energy dominance and expedite deployment of safe, secure, proliferation-resistant U.S. SMRs meeting the highest standards. FIRST provides U.S. SMR expertise to potential buyer countries through training, civil nuclear energy technical tours, site visits, feasibility studies to add U.S. SMRs to buyers' procurement shortlists, SMR control room simulators and training hubs that introduce U.S. SMR technology to emerging nuclear energy markets. Topics include U.S. SMR technology selection, deployment roadmaps, regional collaboration to expedite U.S. SMR fleet deployment, nuclear security, safety, licensing, and nonproliferation, site selection, nuclear workforce development, integrating U.S. SMRs in the energy mix, spent fuel management, etc.

rows.Requirement Title: Promoting Regional Trade Integration and Employment Criteria (PRICE)
rows.Requirement Description: Despite a steady economic growth over the past decades, Laos economy has been mainly driven by large scale and capital intensive sectors such as mining and hydropower which are primarily dominant by Chinese investments. These projects bring considerable environmental costs, cause higher debts, and create less benefits to the people, including knowledge transfer and employment opportunities. The PRICE will therefore focus on enhancing potential of small and micro enterprises (SMEs) in Laos and targeting on  industry, tourism, handicraft and manufacturing sectors. The PRICE aims to (1) foster Lao Business competitiveness and Responsible Investment manner,   (2) build their organizational capacity and quality employment that meet international standards, and (3) advance Lao-U.S trading relationships and their access to U.S and ASEAN markets.
